title: Feeling these heatwaves?
content:
Dear friend ,

It’s been relentless this summer, hasn’t it? These endless heatwaves are a real wake-up call for our councils, showing very clearly that they need to be putting adaptations in place to make our infrastructure more resilient against extreme weather, wildfires and drought.

But don’t sweat. Here’s Isaac from our partners Climate Emergency UK explaining what you can do if you’re feeling powerless in the face of all this heat.

The key is adaptation — the ways in which councils adapt our habitats for resilience, for example by planting more trees, reusing water or making our homes more able to withstand extremes of temperature.

There are useful graphics that explain more on the Council Climate Action Scorecards site. And once you've got that info, take a look to see how your own council is doing, on the main Scorecards section.

While this sun is beating down, it's a great time to go and chat with your councillors about your council's record on adaptation and resilience: why not download these graphics as a conversation-opener?

title: Now WriteToThem is even more helpful
content:
Dear friend ,

We've recently made changes to WriteToThem, our "contact a politician" website, making it easier to do two things:

First, because it can be confusing to figure out which politician to write to, we’ve added new bits of advice that you'll encounter as you use the site, making it easier to get your message to the right person.

And secondly, recognising that WriteToThem has always been an invaluable resource for organisations and charities, we’ve upgraded the options for those using the site to rally support around a campaign (with our usual safeguards around doing so responsibly).

Hop on over to this blog post for all the details.

The improvements described above benefit all WriteToThem users across the UK, but we’ve also been doing work specifically around democratic engagement in Wales.

In a webinar last week, we looked at recent changes to the Senedd, inviting Jess Blair from ERS Cymru to talk through how things look post-election, how the power balance has shifted and how that affects those living in Wales.

After Jess had spoken, mySociety’s Alex explained the changes we’ve made to WriteToThem especially for those with devolved parliaments.

title: AI, government, FOI... and sewage discharges
content:
Dear friend,

Our governments are adopting AI at speed, and we think it should be easier to answer the basic questions: what systems are public bodies using? How are those systems affecting people? Where does accountability lie, when decisions are made in a black box?

We’re embarking on a vital new project, focusing on scrutiny of governments' use of AI. And to kick it off, we brought together experts for an informed discussion about what’s needed. You can read a summary here.

The Information Commissioner’s Office has issued new advice, reflecting the increasing use of AI by those submitting Freedom of Information requests. 

AI brings a new and unique set of challenges to public authorities, many of whom are reporting exceptionally high levels of correspondence. If you'd like to find out how to navigate FOI in this new era of AI, you can read all about it here.

Public opinion does make a difference: it was an increased number of complaints from the public that caused the ICO to take action on sewage data recently, reminding water companies of their obligation to disclose information on discharges: read more here.

title: We have a brand new Prime Minister
content:
Dear friend ,

With all the fuss about Andy Burnham becoming Prime Minister, it may be easy to forget that he’s been in Parliament before — as an MP.

That means that he already had a page on TheyWorkForYou, our website that makes Parliament easier to follow. And, as Burnham originally entered the House in 2001 and didn’t step down until 2017, there’s a lot to explore.

That includes his voting record during that time*.

You can also search Andy Burnham’s speeches, or browse the interests he declared. Of course, all these pages will quickly fill up with new content now that Burnham is Prime Minister.

There’s an easy way to keep up to date with everything that Burnham does in Parliament: click the ‘get email updates’ button at the top of his TheyWorkForYou page, and we’ll send an email when he speaks or votes. This is a free service.

Perhaps you’d like to hear only when he mentions football, railways, wildlife…or anything else you have an interest in. The possibilities are genuinely endless — you can subscribe to as many keywords or phrases as you like.

Here’s how:

  • Go to theyworkforyou.com/alert and click the green button marked ‘create new keyword alert’.

title: Online event: Navigating changes in Welsh democracy with WriteToThem
content: Online event: Navigating changes in Welsh democracy with WriteToThem View this email in your browser Online event Getting the right message to the right place Navigating democracy in Wales with WriteToThem (23rd July: 12-1pm) The democratic map in Wales has changed. Following the 2026 election, people in Wales now have new constituencies for the Senedd with multiple representatives from different parties. WriteToThem exists to solve the problem of who is the right representative to contact. We help people get from their postcode to the right representative: whether that's a councillor, a Member of the Senedd, or a Member of the UK Parliament. In this hour-long event, the mySociety team (and guest speaker Jess Blair from ERS Cymru) will discuss the changing landscape in Wales, and relaunch the service for Wales, walking through what's new, including the new Welsh language version of the service. title: MPs and gifts: the results are in
content:
Dear friend,

Last week, we asked you to share your feelings about MPs receiving gifts — and you certainly told us what you think.

We promised we’d share the results, so here they are:

  • 73.9% say that MPs shouldn’t receive any gifts at all
  • 18.4% think that some types of gift should not be allowed
  • 7.7% told us it’s ok for MPs to receive gifts, so long as they declare them.

    • With gifts and donations to MPs dominating the news headlines, and a new call from the Ethics and Integrity commission for all lobbying to be declared, your responses certainly reflect the national mood.

    92.3% of you believe there should be a change. And we suspect that even those of you who fall within the remaining 7.7% would like to know that the system for MPs declaring gifts is consistently applied.

    That's one of the things we’re pushing for through our WhoFundsThem project.

    “MPs often receive free tickets to expensive and sought-after events such as the Chelsea Flower Show, big pop concerts or high-profile football matches. These come from donors including banks, car manufacturers and the whisky industry.

    “Is this a perk of the job for hardworking MPs, or a step too far?”
snippet:
Dear friend,

title: MPs and gifts: what's ok?
content:
Dear friend,

Thanks to Nigel Farage and the gifts he received from a crypto billionaire, political donations are all over the news again.

It’s not the first such story, nor will it be the last — but whatever your feelings about this particular matter, we believe that standards must be raised around money in politics.

We’ve been looking more closely at the gifts MPs receive. Who do they come from, and is it always fine for our politicians to receive them? We’d love to hear your views.

  • Is it OK for MPs to get paid for making controversial posts on X?
  • is it OK for MPs to receive tickets to sought-after events?
  • should MPs receive any gifts or donations at all?

    • We want to hear what you think: head over to our survey and let us know.

    Better standards start with transparency.

    Through our WhoFundsThem project, we’re working to build better information about the sources of funding politicians receive. We've been exploring links between gifts given to MPs and the questions they ask in Parliament — and a complaint we made, based on what we found, has already resulted in a formal apology from one MP.

title: Together we can push for better access to information
content:
Dear friend,

Last week, Julia braved the heatwave and hopped on the Eurostar to the Netherlands, where she joined campaigners, journalists, lawyers and researchers who work around Freedom of Information, across Europe and beyond.

This was a coming together of the ATI Network Community of Practice — and also a chance to share expertise in advance of the Dutch government’s review of their Open Government Act (charmingly known as “Woo”).

As Julia remarks in her account of the day: “Beyond the work of our own organisations, international attention matters to those in power. Knowing that colleagues across Europe and beyond are following developments, celebrating progress and raising concerns when transparency comes under pressure can strengthen domestic advocacy.

“By continuing to learn from one another, we stand a much better chance of making the right to information work not just on paper, but in practice.”

Read the full blog post here.

Your donations support activity like this, where we can convene organisations who care about transparency, and empower us all by sharing knowledge, experience and skills.
